content.definitionEn: The soft movable part inside the mouth used in tasting, moving food, and forming speech.

examples.en: She touched the loose tooth with her tongue.
examples.vi: Cô ấy dùng lưỡi chạm vào chiếc răng lung lay.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; the tongue can name the organ generally, while my tongue names a person's own.

content.definitionEn: A language, especially one associated with a person's home or community.

examples.en: His grandmother tells stories in her native tongue.
examples.vi: Bà của anh ấy kể chuyện bằng tiếng mẹ đẻ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; native tongue and mother tongue are established expressions. This language use is more literary than language alone.

content.definitionEn: A structure of fine threads made by a spider, often used to catch insects.

examples.en: A web stretched between the two branches above the path.
examples.vi: Một mạng nhện giăng giữa hai cành cây phía trên lối đi.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a spider's web names the structure, not the spider itself.

content.definitionEn: The system of connected pages and resources that people access through the internet.

examples.en: The museum put its opening hours on the web.
examples.vi: Bảo tàng đăng giờ mở cửa lên mạng web.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually the web in this sense; on the web describes online availability. Not every internet service is part of the web.
content.senseLabelEn: linked pages accessed through the internet

content.definitionEn: To work food between your teeth so that it becomes easier to swallow.

examples.en: He chewed the bread slowly while listening to the story.
examples.vi: Anh ấy nhai bánh mì chậm rãi trong lúc nghe câu chuyện.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive chew food or intransitive chew slowly; chew on can also name what is being bitten.

content.definitionEn: Done or experienced repeatedly as part of an established habit.

examples.en: Her habitual early arrival gave her time to unlock the hall.
examples.vi: Thói quen đến sớm thường lệ giúp cô ấy có thời gian mở khóa hội trường.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually before a noun such as behaviour or lateness; repetition does not itself imply addiction.

content.definitionEn: A road vehicle with two wheels that is powered by a motor.

examples.en: They parked the motorcycle beside the repair shop.
examples.vi: Họ đỗ xe máy cạnh tiệm sửa chữa.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; ride a motorcycle describes operating or travelling on it, rather than drive a motorcycle in ordinary usage.

content.definitionEn: Giving a feeling of enjoyment, comfort, or satisfaction.

examples.en: A pleasant breeze cooled the room after lunch.
examples.vi: Một làn gió dễ chịu làm căn phòng mát hơn sau bữa trưa.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a noun or after a linking verb; pleasant describes something enjoyable rather than someone experiencing pleasure.

content.definitionEn: A place where something stands, happens, or is planned to be built.

examples.en: The old factory site will become a public garden.
examples.vi: Khu đất của nhà máy cũ sẽ trở thành một khu vườn công cộng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; site of an event or site for a building specifies the use or association.

content.definitionEn: A website or collection of related pages available online.

examples.en: The charity's site lists places where volunteers are needed.
examples.vi: Trang web của tổ chức từ thiện liệt kê những nơi cần tình nguyện viên.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; visit a site describes online access here, not physical travel.

content.definitionEn: Extending to many parts of the world.

examples.en: The photograph attracted worldwide attention.
examples.vi: Bức ảnh thu hút sự chú ý trên toàn thế giới.

content.grammarNotesEn: Adjective before a noun; worldwide attention describes the geographical reach of interest.

content.definitionEn: In or to places across the world.

examples.en: The company sends its catalogue to readers worldwide.
examples.vi: Công ty gửi danh mục sản phẩm cho độc giả trên khắp thế giới.

content.grammarNotesEn: Adverb modifying distribution or activity; it does not literally require every country or individual.

content.definitionEn: A group of people gathered closely together in a place.

examples.en: A crowd gathered outside the station to welcome the musicians.
examples.vi: Một đám đông tụ tập ngoài nhà ga để chào đón các nhạc công.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable collective noun; a crowd of people specifies its members.

content.definitionEn: More or additional beyond what has already been given or done.

examples.en: Please contact the office for further details.
examples.vi: Hãy liên hệ văn phòng để biết thêm chi tiết.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually before a noun; further information is uncountable, while further questions is plural.

content.definitionEn: At or to a distance beyond the place already reached or mentioned.

examples.en: We walked further along the bank to find a shaded spot.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi đi xa hơn dọc bờ để tìm một chỗ có bóng mát.

content.grammarNotesEn: Adverb with movement or position; this draft concerns distance rather than an additional quantity.

content.definitionEn: Sounds arranged through rhythm, melody, or other patterns for expression or enjoyment.

examples.en: Soft music played while the guests found their seats.
examples.vi: Nhạc nhẹ vang lên trong lúc các vị khách tìm chỗ ngồi.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually uncountable; a piece of music names one work, rather than a music.
content.senseLabelEn: sounds arranged for expression or enjoyment

content.definitionEn: To tear or burst open, or cause something to do so.

examples.en: The frozen pipe ruptured during the night.
examples.vi: Đường ống bị đóng băng vỡ trong đêm.

content.grammarNotesEn: Intransitive something ruptures or transitive rupture something; this example concerns a pipe, not medical advice.

content.definitionEn: The month that follows August and comes before October.

examples.en: The new reading club begins in September.
examples.vi: Câu lạc bộ đọc sách mới bắt đầu vào tháng Chín.

content.grammarNotesEn: Month name written September with a capital S; use in September, but on a particular September date.

content.definitionEn: Each time that something happens.

examples.en: Whenever the door opens, a small bell rings.
examples.vi: Mỗi khi cửa mở, một chiếc chuông nhỏ reo lên.

content.grammarNotesEn: Introduces a clause; the other clause describes what happens on each occasion.

content.definitionEn: At any time that a person chooses or that circumstances allow.

examples.en: You can return the book whenever you finish reading it.
examples.vi: Bạn có thể trả sách bất cứ khi nào đọc xong.

content.grammarNotesEn: Introduces a time clause; present finish can refer to a future occasion after can return.

content.definitionEn: Fine-grained earth that becomes easy to shape when mixed with water and is used for making pottery.

examples.en: The potter pressed the wet clay into a shallow dish.
examples.vi: Thợ gốm ép đất sét ướt thành một chiếc đĩa nông.

content.grammarNotesEn: Uncountable for the material; a piece or lump of clay names an amount.
content.senseLabelEn: fine earth that can be shaped when wet

content.definitionEn: The work or study of using scientific and practical knowledge to design, build, and improve structures or machines.

examples.en: She studies engineering and hopes to design safer bridges.
examples.vi: Cô ấy học ngành kỹ thuật và mong thiết kế những cây cầu an toàn hơn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Uncountable for the field; an engineering project names an application, not an engineering.
content.senseLabelEn: designing and building using technical knowledge

content.definitionEn: Happening or being done without intention, often because something was not noticed.

examples.en: An inadvertent change to the address sent the parcel to another street.
examples.vi: Một thay đổi vô ý ở địa chỉ khiến bưu kiện được gửi sang đường khác.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually before a noun such as error or omission; does not itself mean harmless.

content.definitionEn: To move your head briefly down and up, often to show agreement or recognition.

examples.en: She nodded to show that she had understood the instructions.
examples.vi: Cô ấy gật đầu để cho biết mình đã hiểu hướng dẫn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually intransitive; nod to someone identifies a recipient, and nod one's head uses an object.
content.senseLabelEn: move the head as a signal

content.definitionEn: To let your head drop briefly because you are sleepy.

examples.en: The passenger began to nod as the bus moved through the quiet streets.
examples.vi: Hành khách bắt đầu gật gù vì buồn ngủ khi xe buýt đi qua những con phố yên tĩnh.

content.grammarNotesEn: Intransitive; nod off means begin to fall asleep and is a related phrasal construction.
content.senseLabelEn: let the head drop when sleepy

content.definitionEn: A special chair used by a king, queen, or other ruler on formal occasions.

examples.en: The carved throne stood at the far end of the hall.
examples.vi: Chiếc ngai chạm khắc đặt ở cuối phía bên kia của đại sảnh.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable for the chair; the throne can also refer to royal authority in another use.

content.definitionEn: The measurement of something from one side to the other.

examples.en: Measure the width of the doorway before moving the desk.
examples.vi: Đo chiều rộng cửa ra vào trước khi chuyển chiếc bàn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually the width of something; a width of plus a measurement states its size.

content.definitionEn: A device or sound that warns people about danger or a situation needing attention.

examples.en: The alarm sounded when smoke reached the kitchen sensor.
examples.vi: Chuông báo động reo khi khói tới cảm biến trong bếp.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; set off an alarm means cause it to give a warning.
content.meaningVi: chuông báo động; thiết bị báo hiệu
content.senseLabelEn: device or sound giving a warning

content.definitionEn: To make someone feel worried or afraid about what may happen.

examples.en: The sudden drop in water pressure alarmed the caretaker.
examples.vi: Áp lực nước giảm đột ngột khiến người quản lý tòa nhà lo ngại.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive alarm someone; the cause is the subject and the worried person is the object.
content.meaningVi: làm lo ngại; làm hoảng sợ

content.definitionEn: A feeling of worry or fear when something seems dangerous or wrong.

examples.en: She watched with alarm as the branch bent over the road.
examples.vi: Cô ấy lo sợ nhìn cành cây cong xuống phía trên con đường.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually uncountable in with alarm or cause alarm; distinct from a warning device.
content.meaningVi: sự lo sợ; sự hoảng hốt

content.definitionEn: Used in and so forth to suggest more items of the kind already mentioned.

examples.en: Bring pencils, paper, glue, and so forth for the craft session.
examples.vi: Hãy mang bút chì, giấy, keo dán, vân vân cho buổi làm đồ thủ công.

content.grammarNotesEn: This sense occurs in the phrase and so forth after a list; forth alone does not mean et cetera.
content.meaningVi: vân vân; và những thứ tương tự

content.definitionEn: Out from a place or forwards from a starting point.

examples.en: Music came forth from the open doorway.
examples.vi: Tiếng nhạc vọng ra từ ô cửa đang mở.

content.grammarNotesEn: Formal or literary after movement or emergence verbs; back and forth describes repeated movement in opposite directions.
content.senseLabelEn: out or forwards from a place

content.definitionEn: To become greater in amount, size, or number, or make something greater.

examples.en: The library increased its opening hours during the exam period.
examples.vi: Thư viện tăng giờ mở cửa trong kỳ thi.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive increase something or intransitive something increases; increase by gives the change and increase to gives the new level.

content.definitionEn: A rise in the amount, size, or number of something.

examples.en: There was an increase in visitors after the exhibition opened.
examples.vi: Số khách tăng lên sau khi triển lãm mở cửa.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable in an increase in something; by/to distinguish the amount of change from the resulting level.

content.definitionEn: To go back to a place where you were before.

examples.en: We returned to the village before the evening rain.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi trở về làng trước cơn mưa chiều.

content.grammarNotesEn: Intransitive return to a place; return home has no to before home.
content.senseLabelEn: go back to an earlier place

content.definitionEn: The act of coming back to a place or situation.

examples.en: Her return to the choir pleased the other singers.
examples.vi: Việc cô ấy trở lại dàn hợp xướng khiến các ca sĩ khác vui mừng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually a return to something; possessive forms such as her return identify who comes back.
content.meaningVi: sự trở về; lần quay lại

content.definitionEn: To give or send something back to its owner or an earlier place.

examples.en: Please return the borrowed tools to the shed.
examples.vi: Hãy trả những dụng cụ đã mượn về nhà kho.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive return something to someone or somewhere; the object is what is given back.

content.definitionEn: To find a person, thing, or origin by following available signs or evidence.

examples.en: They traced the missing parcel to a neighbouring shop.
examples.vi: Họ lần theo dấu vết và tìm được bưu kiện thất lạc ở cửa hàng bên cạnh.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive trace something to a place or source; the endpoint is introduced by to.
content.meaningVi: truy tìm; lần theo dấu vết

content.definitionEn: A sign left by something that was present or happened earlier.

examples.en: The muddy floor showed traces of the visitors' boots.
examples.vi: Sàn nhà lấm bùn có dấu vết giày của các vị khách.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; traces of something are signs of its earlier presence.
content.senseLabelEn: small sign that something was present

content.definitionEn: A very small amount of a substance or quality.

examples.en: There was a trace of paint on his sleeve.
examples.vi: Có một vệt sơn rất nhỏ trên tay áo của anh ấy.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable in a trace of; emphasizes a small amount rather than a complete absence.

content.definitionEn: To copy a drawing by following its lines through or on another surface.

examples.en: She traced the leaf shape onto thin paper.
examples.vi: Cô ấy đồ lại hình chiếc lá lên giấy mỏng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive trace a shape onto a surface; distinct from finding something through evidence.

content.definitionEn: The process of becoming warmer or increasing in temperature.

examples.en: The warming of the room was gradual after the heater came on.
examples.vi: Căn phòng ấm dần lên sau khi máy sưởi bật.

content.grammarNotesEn: Uncountable process noun; warming of names what becomes warmer. Global warming is a specific context rather than the only meaning.
content.meaningVi: sự nóng lên; sự ấm lên

content.definitionEn: A person who controls a car or other road vehicle while it is moving.

examples.en: The driver waited until everyone had fastened their seat belt.
examples.vi: Tài xế chờ cho đến khi mọi người thắt dây an toàn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; driver of a vehicle names the person operating it, not every passenger.

content.definitionEn: Having the same or very similar composition or characteristics throughout.

examples.en: Stir the mixture until it looks homogeneous.
examples.vi: Khuấy hỗn hợp cho đến khi trông đồng nhất.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a noun or after a linking verb; homogeneity concerns uniform composition, not moral agreement.
content.meaningVi: đồng nhất; tương đối đồng đều

content.definitionEn: Not showing interest or concern about someone or something.

examples.en: He seemed indifferent to the choice of restaurant.
examples.vi: Anh ấy có vẻ không quan tâm đến việc chọn nhà hàng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Indifferent to names what causes little interest; this sense does not necessarily mean actively hostile.

content.definitionEn: A device that receives broadcasts of speech or music.

examples.en: She turned the radio down so she could hear the knock.
examples.vi: Cô ấy vặn nhỏ tiếng đài để nghe tiếng gõ cửa.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable for the device; turn the radio down reduces volume, not its physical position.

content.definitionEn: The medium of broadcasting sound programmes to listeners.

examples.en: The interview will be broadcast on local radio tomorrow.
examples.vi: Cuộc phỏng vấn sẽ được phát trên đài địa phương vào ngày mai.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually uncountable; on the radio refers to broadcast availability rather than a device's surface.

content.definitionEn: A person's own identity, character, and inner experience.

examples.en: The journal helped her understand her own self more clearly.
examples.vi: Cuốn nhật ký giúp cô ấy hiểu bản thân rõ hơn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable in phrases such as one's true self; selves is the plural. This noun differs from reflexive pronouns such as herself.
content.meaningVi: bản thân; con người bên trong

content.definitionEn: Made from wood.

examples.en: A wooden bench stood under the old mango tree.
examples.vi: Một chiếc ghế dài bằng gỗ đặt dưới cây xoài già.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a noun or after a linking verb; this material sense differs from wooden meaning stiff or unexpressive.

content.definitionEn: A member of a council that makes decisions for a local area.

examples.en: The councillor listened to residents' concerns about the crossing.
examples.vi: Thành viên hội đồng địa phương lắng nghe lo ngại của cư dân về chỗ qua đường.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; British spelling councillor, American councilor. Counsellor refers to a different role.
content.meaningVi: thành viên hội đồng địa phương; nghị viên địa phương

content.definitionEn: To consider evidence in order to judge the quality, value, or effectiveness of something.

examples.en: The teachers evaluated the new timetable after a month.
examples.vi: Các giáo viên đánh giá thời khóa biểu mới sau một tháng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive evaluate something; evaluation may examine strengths and weaknesses, not only assign a score.

content.definitionEn: Among the most important, successful, or influential in a particular area.

examples.en: A leading researcher spoke at the public lecture.
examples.vi: Một nhà nghiên cứu hàng đầu phát biểu tại buổi diễn thuyết công cộng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually before a noun; a leading person need not be the only leader or the person physically in front.
content.senseLabelEn: among the most important or successful

content.definitionEn: The act of watching something carefully to learn about it.

examples.en: Careful observation revealed which birds visited the garden first.
examples.vi: Sự quan sát kỹ cho thấy những loài chim nào đến khu vườn trước.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually uncountable for the process; observation of names what is watched.

content.definitionEn: A comment about something that someone has noticed.

examples.en: Her observation about the crowded entrance led us to move the sign.
examples.vi: Nhận xét của cô ấy về lối vào đông đúc khiến chúng tôi chuyển biển chỉ dẫn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; make an observation about something introduces a particular comment.

content.definitionEn: The number that is one greater than twelve.

examples.en: Thirteen chairs fitted around the long table.
examples.vi: Mười ba chiếc ghế kê vừa quanh chiếc bàn dài.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a plural count noun or used alone as a number; thirteen chairs takes plural agreement.

content.definitionEn: To form written words or compose a text using handwriting, typing, or another writing method.

examples.en: She wrote a short note explaining where the keys were.
examples.vi: Cô ấy viết một ghi chú ngắn giải thích chìa khóa ở đâu.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive write a text; write to someone names the recipient. Past wrote and past participle written.

content.definitionEn: An unexpected event that causes damage, injury, or another unwanted result.

examples.en: A minor accident blocked the narrow road for an hour.
examples.vi: Một tai nạn nhỏ làm tắc con đường hẹp trong một giờ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; have an accident names the event, while by accident expresses lack of intention.
content.senseLabelEn: unexpected event causing damage or injury

content.definitionEn: Something that happens by chance rather than being planned.

examples.en: Meeting her at the book fair was a happy accident.
examples.vi: Gặp cô ấy ở hội chợ sách là một sự tình cờ vui vẻ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable in a happy accident; by accident means unintentionally and need not involve injury.
content.meaningVi: sự tình cờ; chuyện ngoài dự định

content.definitionEn: Relating to a system in which a central government shares authority with constituent states, or to that central government.

examples.en: The class compared federal and local responsibilities in a fictional country.
examples.vi: Lớp học so sánh trách nhiệm của chính quyền liên bang và địa phương ở một quốc gia giả định.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually before a noun such as government or authority; not a synonym for every national government.
content.senseLabelEn: relating to a federation's central government

content.definitionEn: To make someone feel afraid or less confident, sometimes to influence their behaviour.

examples.en: The aggressive questions intimidated the new speaker.
examples.vi: Những câu hỏi gay gắt khiến người diễn giả mới mất tự tin.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive intimidate someone; intimidate someone into doing something names an action induced by pressure.
content.meaningVi: đe dọa; làm sợ; gây áp lực khiến mất tự tin
content.senseLabelEn: make someone afraid or less confident

content.definitionEn: A team sport in which players carry, pass, and kick an oval ball to score.

examples.en: The school rugby team practised passing on the field.
examples.vi: Đội rugby của trường tập chuyền bóng trên sân.

content.grammarNotesEn: Uncountable when naming the sport; a rugby match is countable. Rugby is distinct from American football.
content.meaningVi: môn rugby; bóng bầu dục rugby
content.senseLabelEn: team sport with an oval ball

content.definitionEn: Easily affected by emotions, criticism, or how others behave.

examples.en: She is sensitive to criticism about her artwork.
examples.vi: Cô ấy nhạy cảm với những lời phê bình về tác phẩm của mình.

content.grammarNotesEn: Sensitive to names the cause of an emotional response; does not necessarily mean unreasonable.
content.meaningVi: nhạy cảm; dễ bị tổn thương về cảm xúc
content.senseLabelEn: easily affected by feelings or treatment

content.definitionEn: Able to detect or be affected by small changes or particular conditions.

examples.en: The sensor is sensitive to small changes in light.
examples.vi: Cảm biến nhạy với những thay đổi nhỏ của ánh sáng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Sensitive to identifies the stimulus; the subject may be a device, material, or body part.

content.definitionEn: Showing sound judgment based on understanding or experience.

examples.en: It was wise to check the route before leaving.
examples.vi: Kiểm tra lộ trình trước khi đi là một việc làm sáng suốt.

content.grammarNotesEn: A wise decision or it is wise to do something evaluates judgment; not restricted to older people.

content.definitionEn: A plan showing how something should look, be built, or function.

examples.en: The design includes a ramp beside the front steps.
examples.vi: Bản thiết kế có một lối dốc cạnh các bậc thềm phía trước.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable for a particular plan; uncountable for the activity or field of designing.
content.senseLabelEn: plan for how something will look or work

content.definitionEn: To plan the appearance, structure, or operation of something before it is made.

examples.en: The students designed a box that could be folded flat.
examples.vi: Học sinh thiết kế một chiếc hộp có thể gấp phẳng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive design something; design something for a purpose identifies its intended use.
content.senseLabelEn: plan the form or function of something

content.definitionEn: To take place or occur.

examples.en: The power cut happened just before the concert began.
examples.vi: Sự cố mất điện xảy ra ngay trước khi buổi hòa nhạc bắt đầu.

content.grammarNotesEn: Intransitive; what happened asks about an event, while happen to someone names who experiences it.

content.definitionEn: To do or be something by chance rather than because it was arranged.

examples.en: I happened to meet our old neighbour at the station.
examples.vi: Tôi tình cờ gặp người hàng xóm cũ ở nhà ga.

content.grammarNotesEn: Happen to plus an infinitive expresses chance; the infinitive need not describe a harmful event.

content.definitionEn: Special or striking enough to be remembered for a long time.

examples.en: The children gave a memorable performance at the village festival.
examples.vi: Bọn trẻ có một màn biểu diễn đáng nhớ tại lễ hội của làng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a noun or after a linking verb; memorable can describe good or bad experiences.

content.definitionEn: To forbid an activity or prevent it through a rule or authority.

examples.en: The gallery rules prohibit flash photography.
examples.vi: Nội quy phòng trưng bày cấm chụp ảnh có đèn flash.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive prohibit an activity; prohibit someone from doing something names the person and forbidden action.

content.definitionEn: A person who does not eat meat or fish.

examples.en: The vegetarian in our group chose a bean dish.
examples.vi: Người ăn chay trong nhóm chúng tôi chọn một món đậu.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; some vegetarians eat eggs or dairy products, unlike vegans. This record proposes the person noun.

content.definitionEn: Having many trees growing over an area.

examples.en: A wooded hillside sheltered the houses from the wind.
examples.vi: Một sườn đồi nhiều cây che chắn những ngôi nhà khỏi gió.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually before a place noun; wooded describes tree cover, while wooden describes material.
content.meaningVi: có nhiều cây; phủ cây rừng

content.definitionEn: An event that includes formal or traditional actions to mark an occasion.

examples.en: The ceremony began with a short welcome from the organiser.
examples.vi: Buổi lễ bắt đầu bằng lời chào mừng ngắn của người tổ chức.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a ceremony can mark a happy or solemn occasion and need not be religious.

content.definitionEn: To leave someone or something out of a group, list, or calculation.

examples.en: The price excludes delivery to remote addresses.
examples.vi: Giá không bao gồm giao hàng đến các địa chỉ xa xôi.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive exclude something; an excluded item is not part of the stated set or total.
content.senseLabelEn: leave out of a set or amount

content.definitionEn: To prevent someone from entering or taking part in something.

examples.en: The rule excludes younger children from the evening activity.
examples.vi: Quy định không cho trẻ nhỏ hơn tham gia hoạt động buổi tối.

content.grammarNotesEn: Exclude someone from plus an activity or group; the person is the direct object.
content.meaningVi: không cho tham gia; loại trừ

content.definitionEn: A strap, cord, or chain attached to an animal to keep it under control.

examples.en: He shortened the dog's leash near the busy crossing.
examples.vi: Anh ấy thu ngắn dây dắt chó gần chỗ qua đường đông đúc.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; on a leash means restrained by the lead, not carried on top of it.
content.meaningVi: dây dắt; dây xích thú nuôi
content.senseLabelEn: strap or cord for controlling an animal

content.definitionEn: The state of being close to something in distance, time, or relationship.

examples.en: The flat's proximity to the station made the journey easier.
examples.vi: Căn hộ ở gần nhà ga nên việc đi lại thuận tiện hơn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Uncountable; proximity to names what is nearby, often in formal writing.

content.definitionEn: The loud rumbling or crashing sound heard during a storm in connection with lightning.

examples.en: A sudden clap of thunder interrupted the conversation.
examples.vi: Một tiếng sấm đột ngột làm gián đoạn cuộc trò chuyện.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually uncountable; a clap or roll of thunder names one sound or sequence.

content.definitionEn: Having repeated gentle curves rather than being straight.

examples.en: She drew a wavy line below the heading.
examples.vi: Cô ấy vẽ một đường lượn sóng dưới tiêu đề.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a noun or after a linking verb; wavy hair describes curved shape, not wetness.

content.definitionEn: Of a reasonably good standard or sufficient for a need.

examples.en: We found a decent room within our budget.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi tìm được một phòng khá tốt trong khả năng chi trả.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a noun or after a linking verb; decent need not mean excellent.

content.definitionEn: Behaving in a fair, respectful, or morally acceptable way.

examples.en: It was decent of him to return the lost wallet.
examples.vi: Anh ấy thật tử tế khi trả lại chiếc ví bị mất.

content.grammarNotesEn: Decent of someone to do something evaluates an action; distinct from adequate quality.

content.definitionEn: Able to stretch under force and return towards the previous shape when the force is removed.

examples.en: The elastic cuff stretched easily over her hand.
examples.vi: Cổ tay áo co giãn dễ dàng giãn ra để bàn tay cô ấy luồn qua.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a material or object noun; elastic here is an adjective, not the related material noun.
content.senseLabelEn: able to stretch and return towards its shape

content.definitionEn: Causing strong feelings, especially sympathy or sadness.

examples.en: Her account of the reunion was deeply moving.
examples.vi: Lời kể của cô ấy về cuộc đoàn tụ rất cảm động.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a noun or after a linking verb; moving describes the cause, while moved can describe the affected person.

content.definitionEn: Changing position rather than remaining still.

examples.en: The photographer waited for the moving boat to pass.
examples.vi: Nhiếp ảnh gia chờ chiếc thuyền đang di chuyển đi qua.

content.grammarNotesEn: Participial adjective before a noun in this sense; not the emotional meaning.
content.meaningVi: đang chuyển động; đang di chuyển

content.definitionEn: To arrange for something planned to happen later than originally intended.

examples.en: They postponed the outdoor concert until the following weekend.
examples.vi: Họ hoãn buổi hòa nhạc ngoài trời đến cuối tuần sau.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive postpone an event; postpone doing something uses an ing form, and until introduces the later time.
content.senseLabelEn: move a planned event to a later time

content.definitionEn: To go to a person or place in order to spend time there.

examples.en: We visited the local museum during the school break.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi đến thăm bảo tàng địa phương trong kỳ nghỉ học.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive visit a place or person; a visit to uses to in the noun construction.

content.definitionEn: An occasion when someone goes to a person or place and spends time there.

examples.en: Her first visit to the island lasted a week.
examples.vi: Chuyến thăm hòn đảo đầu tiên của cô ấy kéo dài một tuần.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; pay a visit to someone or somewhere describes making such a visit.
content.senseLabelEn: occasion spent at a place or with someone

content.definitionEn: The number representing no amount, or the point from which a scale is measured.

examples.en: The display showed zero messages in the inbox.
examples.vi: Màn hình hiển thị không có tin nhắn nào trong hộp thư đến.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a count noun or used alone as a number; zero messages is plural despite the absence of messages.

content.definitionEn: Having a low temperature, or feeling a lack of warmth.

examples.en: The cold floor made us look for our slippers.
examples.vi: Sàn nhà lạnh khiến chúng tôi tìm dép đi trong nhà.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a noun or after a linking verb; feel cold describes a person's sensation.

content.definitionEn: A common illness often involving a runny or blocked nose and a sore throat.

examples.en: He stayed home because he had a cold.
examples.vi: Anh ấy ở nhà vì bị cảm lạnh.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; have or catch a cold. This noun is distinct from cold weather.

content.definitionEn: An attractive smoothness and control in the way someone moves.

examples.en: The dancer crossed the stage with effortless grace.
examples.vi: Vũ công bước ngang sân khấu với vẻ thanh thoát tự nhiên.

content.grammarNotesEn: Uncountable; with grace describes the quality of movement, not an individual step.
content.meaningVi: sự duyên dáng; vẻ thanh thoát

content.definitionEn: Kind, courteous, and composed behaviour towards others, especially in a difficult situation.

examples.en: She accepted the disappointing result with grace.
examples.vi: Cô ấy đón nhận kết quả đáng thất vọng một cách điềm đạm.

content.grammarNotesEn: Uncountable in with grace; concerns manner of conduct rather than physical movement.
content.meaningVi: sự nhã nhặn; sự điềm đạm

content.definitionEn: A person regarded as having a lower rank or position than another person.

examples.en: The officer refused to speak harshly to his inferiors.
examples.vi: Viên sĩ quan không chịu nói năng gay gắt với những người cấp dưới.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable and often disapproving or hierarchical; the term describes rank in this sense, not human worth.
content.meaningVi: người ở cấp thấp hơn; cấp dưới

content.definitionEn: A person who publicly shows opposition to an action, policy, or situation.

examples.en: A protester held a sign asking for cleaner water.
examples.vi: Một người biểu tình cầm biển yêu cầu nước sạch hơn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; protester against a policy identifies the object of opposition, but not every protester belongs to one organization.
content.meaningVi: người biểu tình; người phản đối công khai

content.definitionEn: Relating to the bones that form the supporting framework of a body.

examples.en: The diagram labels the main skeletal structures.
examples.vi: Sơ đồ ghi tên các cấu trúc chính của bộ xương.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually before a noun such as structure or system; this sense concerns anatomy rather than an extremely thin appearance.
content.meaningVi: thuộc bộ xương; liên quan đến xương

content.definitionEn: The determination to control your actions and keep working towards a chosen goal.

examples.en: It took willpower to keep practising when progress was slow.
examples.vi: Cần có ý chí để tiếp tục luyện tập khi tiến bộ chậm.

content.grammarNotesEn: Uncountable; willpower can support persistence but does not guarantee success or remove every obstacle.
content.meaningVi: ý chí; sức mạnh tự chủ

content.definitionEn: A musical instrument played by striking a stretched surface, usually over a hollow body.

examples.en: The drummer tapped the drum softly before the song began.
examples.vi: Người chơi trống gõ nhẹ lên trống trước khi bài hát bắt đầu.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; play the drums commonly refers to a set of percussion instruments.
content.senseLabelEn: instrument played by striking a stretched surface

content.definitionEn: Very strong or intense, especially in force or competition.

examples.en: A fierce wind pushed against the windows all night.
examples.vi: Một cơn gió dữ dội thổi vào các cửa sổ suốt đêm.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a noun or after a linking verb; fierce competition concerns intensity rather than an animal's aggression.

content.definitionEn: Showing strong aggression or appearing ready to attack.

examples.en: The fierce dog growled when strangers approached the gate.
examples.vi: Con chó hung dữ gầm gừ khi người lạ đến gần cổng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Can describe an animal, person, or expression; appearance alone need not establish that an attack occurs.
content.senseLabelEn: ready to attack or show anger

content.definitionEn: To a great extent or for the most part.

examples.en: The event was largely organised by volunteers.
examples.vi: Sự kiện chủ yếu do các tình nguyện viên tổ chức.

content.grammarNotesEn: Modifies a clause, verb phrase, or adjective; largely allows exceptions and does not mean completely.

content.definitionEn: An image of something seen in a mirror or another reflective surface.

examples.en: She saw the bridge's reflection in the still water.
examples.vi: Cô ấy thấy hình ảnh cây cầu phản chiếu trong mặt nước phẳng lặng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; reflection in a surface names the image's location.
content.senseLabelEn: image seen in a reflective surface

content.definitionEn: Careful thought about an experience, question, or decision.

examples.en: After some reflection, he decided to revise the plan.
examples.vi: Sau khi suy ngẫm, anh ấy quyết định chỉnh sửa kế hoạch.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually uncountable for the process; on reflection means after thinking further.
content.meaningVi: sự suy ngẫm; sự cân nhắc

content.definitionEn: Money that a public authority requires people or organizations to pay to fund public services or activities.

examples.en: The receipt shows the price and the tax separately.
examples.vi: Biên lai ghi giá và thuế riêng biệt.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable for a type or payment, and uncountable in pay tax; no particular rate is implied.

content.definitionEn: To require a person, income, or transaction to pay tax.

examples.en: The fictional city taxes some commercial activities.
examples.vi: Thành phố giả định đánh thuế một số hoạt động thương mại.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive tax a person or activity; the subject is the authority imposing the payment.
content.senseLabelEn: require a tax payment on something

content.definitionEn: Any person who does something or meets a stated condition.

examples.en: Whoever arrives first can choose a seat.
examples.vi: Ai đến trước có thể chọn chỗ ngồi.

content.grammarNotesEn: Introduces a clause acting as a noun phrase; in formal questions who and whoever have different functions.
content.senseLabelEn: any person who meets a condition

content.definitionEn: Used for an unspecified amount or number, often in a question or negative statement.

examples.en: Have you received any letters this week?
examples.vi: Tuần này bạn có nhận được lá thư nào không?

content.grammarNotesEn: Before plural count nouns or uncountable nouns in this use; questions and negatives are common, not the only uses of any.
content.senseLabelEn: an unspecified amount or even one

content.definitionEn: Used to say that it does not matter which member of a group is chosen.

examples.en: You may use any chair in this room.
examples.vi: Bạn có thể dùng bất kỳ chiếc ghế nào trong phòng này.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before singular or plural count nouns in free-choice use; differs from an unspecified quantity in a question.

content.definitionEn: One or some members of a group, without naming which.

examples.en: We have spare notebooks if you need any.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi có vở dự phòng nếu bạn cần một ít.

content.grammarNotesEn: Used without a following noun when the thing is understood; any of plus a defined group is another pronoun construction.
content.meaningVi: cái nào; một ít; bất kỳ cái nào
content.senseLabelEn: one or some without specifying which

content.definitionEn: To even a small extent, especially with a comparison in a question or negative statement.

examples.en: The second attempt was not any easier.
examples.vi: Lần thử thứ hai chẳng dễ hơn chút nào.

content.grammarNotesEn: Degree adverb before a comparative such as easier or better; does not modify a noun as a determiner here.

content.definitionEn: Feeling or showing thanks for something helpful or beneficial.

examples.en: We were grateful for the neighbours' help with the move.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi biết ơn sự giúp đỡ của hàng xóm khi chuyển nhà.

content.grammarNotesEn: Grateful to a person for something; grateful for a benefit. Not the same as pleased that something exists.
content.senseLabelEn: feeling thanks for help or benefit

content.definitionEn: A substance that flows and takes the shape of its container rather than keeping a fixed shape.

examples.en: She poured the liquid carefully into a narrow bottle.
examples.vi: Cô ấy cẩn thận rót chất lỏng vào một chai cổ hẹp.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable for a type of substance; uncountable in quantities such as a litre of liquid.
content.senseLabelEn: substance that flows and takes its container's shape

content.definitionEn: In a physical state that can flow and take the shape of a container.

examples.en: The wax was still liquid when he poured it into the mould.
examples.vi: Sáp vẫn ở dạng lỏng khi anh ấy đổ vào khuôn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a material noun or after a linking verb; liquid here describes physical state, not financial availability.

content.definitionEn: An occasion when people present music, drama, or another artistic work to an audience.

examples.en: The performance ended with a song by the whole cast.
examples.vi: Buổi biểu diễn kết thúc bằng một bài hát của toàn bộ diễn viên.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a performance of a work names what is presented.
content.meaningVi: buổi biểu diễn; màn trình diễn

content.definitionEn: How well a person, machine, or system carries out an activity.

examples.en: The new battery improved the camera's performance.
examples.vi: Pin mới cải thiện hiệu suất hoạt động của máy ảnh.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually uncountable for quality of operation; performance in a task identifies the context.
content.meaningVi: hiệu suất; mức độ thực hiện
content.senseLabelEn: quality of someone's work or operation

content.definitionEn: A single thin length of something such as hair, thread, or wire.

examples.en: A strand of hair had caught on the scarf.
examples.vi: Một sợi tóc mắc vào chiếc khăn quàng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a strand of specifies the material, while strands is the plural.

content.definitionEn: One part or line of activity within a larger, interconnected whole.

examples.en: The project combines a research strand with public workshops.
examples.vi: Dự án kết hợp một mảng nghiên cứu với các buổi hội thảo công cộng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a strand of a project or argument names a connected component, not a physical fibre.
content.senseLabelEn: one connected part of a larger whole

content.definitionEn: Used before a noun to ask which person owns or is associated with something.

examples.en: Whose bag is beside the door?
examples.vi: Chiếc túi cạnh cửa là của ai?

content.grammarNotesEn: Question determiner before a noun; whose is a possession word, while who's means who is or who has.

content.definitionEn: Used to ask who owns something when the thing is already understood.

examples.en: Several coats are here; whose is this?
examples.vi: Ở đây có vài chiếc áo khoác; chiếc này là của ai?

content.grammarNotesEn: Standalone question pronoun; no noun follows whose in this construction.
content.senseLabelEn: asking the owner without repeating the noun

content.definitionEn: Used to connect a person or thing with something belonging or related to it.

examples.en: We met a writer whose stories are set by the sea.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi gặp một nhà văn có những câu chuyện lấy bối cảnh bên biển.

content.grammarNotesEn: Relative determiner before a noun; can refer to people or things and does not require an apostrophe.
content.meaningVi: có; mà của người đó hoặc vật đó
content.senseLabelEn: linking a person or thing to a possession

content.definitionEn: Extremely bad, unpleasant, or upsetting.

examples.en: The awful smell made us open every window.
examples.vi: Mùi kinh khủng khiến chúng tôi mở tất cả cửa sổ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a noun or after a linking verb; stronger than simply not good.

content.definitionEn: A unit of inherited information carried in DNA that helps direct biological functions and characteristics.

examples.en: The lesson explained how a gene can affect the production of a protein.
examples.vi: Bài học giải thích cách một gen có thể ảnh hưởng đến việc tạo ra một protein.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a gene may influence a characteristic, but many characteristics depend on multiple genes and other factors.

content.definitionEn: The opening part of a text or talk that gives background and prepares the audience for what follows.

examples.en: The introduction explains why the survey was conducted.
examples.vi: Phần mở đầu giải thích vì sao cuộc khảo sát được thực hiện.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; introduction to a text or subject identifies what is introduced.
content.meaningVi: phần mở đầu; phần giới thiệu

content.definitionEn: The act of telling people who someone is so that they can become acquainted.

examples.en: After a brief introduction, the visitors began asking questions.
examples.vi: Sau phần giới thiệu làm quen ngắn, các vị khách bắt đầu đặt câu hỏi.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable for an occasion; make introductions is commonly plural when presenting several people.

content.definitionEn: The act of making something available or putting it into use for the first time in a context.

examples.en: The introduction of online booking reduced queues at the desk.
examples.vi: Việc áp dụng đặt chỗ trực tuyến làm giảm hàng người chờ ở quầy.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually introduction of something into a setting; this process sense differs from the opening of a book.
content.meaningVi: sự đưa vào; việc áp dụng
content.senseLabelEn: bringing something into use or a place

content.definitionEn: Showing prejudice or unfair treatment towards people because of their race or perceived racial identity.

examples.en: The school removed a racist slogan from the noticeboard.
examples.vi: Nhà trường gỡ bỏ một khẩu hiệu phân biệt chủng tộc khỏi bảng thông báo.

content.grammarNotesEn: Can describe language, beliefs, actions, or practices; refers to discrimination, not merely mentioning race.
content.senseLabelEn: showing prejudice or unfair treatment based on race

content.definitionEn: A person who holds or expresses prejudice against people because of their race.

examples.en: The speaker challenged a racist who had insulted the visitors.
examples.vi: Diễn giả phản bác một người phân biệt chủng tộc đã xúc phạm các vị khách.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; an evaluative term about beliefs or behaviour, not a person's racial identity.
content.meaningVi: người có tư tưởng hoặc hành vi phân biệt chủng tộc

content.definitionEn: A small natural flow of water through the land.

examples.en: We crossed the stream on a narrow wooden bridge.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi băng qua con suối bằng một cây cầu gỗ hẹp.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a stream is generally smaller than a river, with no single size rule implied.

content.definitionEn: A continuing flow or sequence of people, things, or events.

examples.en: A stream of visitors entered the exhibition throughout the afternoon.
examples.vi: Một dòng khách liên tục vào triển lãm suốt buổi chiều.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable in a stream of plus a plural or mass noun; need not involve water.
content.meaningVi: dòng liên tục; chuỗi liên tiếp

content.definitionEn: A fault or limitation that makes a person or thing less effective.

examples.en: The review identified a weakness in the booking process.
examples.vi: Bản đánh giá chỉ ra một điểm yếu trong quy trình đặt chỗ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable for a particular limitation; weakness in names the affected area.

content.definitionEn: The state of having little strength or power.

examples.en: After the long journey, he felt weakness in his legs.
examples.vi: Sau chuyến đi dài, anh ấy cảm thấy chân yếu đi.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually uncountable for the condition; distinct from a countable fault in a plan.
content.meaningVi: sự yếu đi; tình trạng yếu sức
content.senseLabelEn: lack of physical or other strength

content.definitionEn: The part of the face that projects below the lower lip.

examples.en: She rested her chin on her hand while reading.
examples.vi: Cô ấy tựa cằm lên tay trong lúc đọc sách.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; under one's chin identifies a position beneath this part of the face.
content.senseLabelEn: part of the face below the mouth

content.definitionEn: A large round citrus fruit with juicy flesh that often tastes tart and slightly bitter.

examples.en: He cut a grapefruit in half and placed it in a small bowl.
examples.vi: Anh ấy bổ đôi một quả bưởi chùm rồi đặt vào một chiếc bát nhỏ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable for a whole fruit; uncountable for its flesh as food. Grapefruit is distinct from the larger pomelo.

content.definitionEn: The central part or position between the ends or sides of something.

examples.en: A low table stood in the middle of the room.
examples.vi: Một chiếc bàn thấp đặt ở giữa phòng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Often the middle of something; in the middle locates something centrally or within a sequence.

content.definitionEn: Situated between the outer parts or between the beginning and end.

examples.en: The middle shelf holds the books we use most often.
examples.vi: Kệ ở giữa đựng những cuốn sách chúng tôi dùng thường xuyên nhất.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually before a noun; middle identifies relative position rather than an exact numerical midpoint.

content.definitionEn: A place by the sea or another navigable waterway where ships stop to load or unload.

examples.en: The ship reached the port shortly before dawn.
examples.vi: Con tàu đến cảng ngay trước bình minh.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable for a harbour or town; in port and leave port often omit an article.
content.senseLabelEn: place where ships load and unload

content.definitionEn: A large area of land considered as one piece.

examples.en: The council set aside a tract of land for a public park.
examples.vi: Hội đồng dành riêng một vùng đất để làm công viên công cộng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a tract of land is the usual construction. Anatomical tract and short written tract are different senses.

content.definitionEn: The health, comfort, and good living conditions of a person or group.

examples.en: The organisation puts the welfare of its workers first.
examples.vi: Tổ chức đặt phúc lợi của người lao động lên hàng đầu.

content.grammarNotesEn: Uncountable; welfare of someone concerns their well-being, not necessarily a government payment.
content.meaningVi: phúc lợi; sự an lành; đời sống tốt đẹp

content.definitionEn: Support provided through public systems for people who need help with basic living needs.

examples.en: The office explains how residents can apply for welfare.
examples.vi: Văn phòng giải thích cách cư dân có thể xin hỗ trợ an sinh.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually uncountable; welfare benefits names forms of support. Eligibility depends on the particular system.
content.meaningVi: trợ cấp xã hội; hỗ trợ an sinh
content.senseLabelEn: public support for people in need

content.definitionEn: Having a very large or extreme effect on a situation.

examples.en: The shortage forced a drastic reduction in opening hours.
examples.vi: Tình trạng thiếu hụt buộc phải cắt giảm mạnh giờ mở cửa.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually before a noun such as change or reduction; drastic need not involve violence.
content.meaningVi: mạnh mẽ; quyết liệt; sâu rộng
content.senseLabelEn: having a large or extreme effect

content.definitionEn: Happening often or at repeated short intervals.

examples.en: Frequent delays made the morning journey difficult.
examples.vi: Những lần chậm trễ thường xuyên khiến chuyến đi buổi sáng khó khăn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Adjective before a noun or after a linking verb; frequently is the related adverb.

content.definitionEn: To supply water to land or crops so that plants can grow.

examples.en: Farmers irrigated the dry fields using a narrow channel.
examples.vi: Nông dân tưới các cánh đồng khô bằng một con mương hẹp.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive irrigate land or crops; the land is the object, not the person receiving water.
content.meaningVi: tưới tiêu; tưới nước cho đất trồng
content.senseLabelEn: supply land with water for growing plants

content.definitionEn: To adapt something to a particular person's needs or preferences.

examples.en: The tutor personalised the exercises for each learner.
examples.vi: Gia sư điều chỉnh các bài tập cho từng người học.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive personalize something for someone; personalise is the usual British spelling.
content.meaningVi: cá nhân hóa; điều chỉnh cho từng người
content.senseLabelEn: adapt to an individual's needs or preferences

content.definitionEn: The act of giving up something valuable, or the thing given up, to help someone or achieve another aim.

examples.en: Moving closer to work involved a sacrifice of living space.
examples.vi: Chuyển đến gần nơi làm việc đồng nghĩa với việc đánh đổi diện tích ở.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable for a particular loss or act; sacrifice of something names what is given up.
content.meaningVi: sự hy sinh; điều phải đánh đổi
content.senseLabelEn: something valuable given up for another purpose

content.definitionEn: To give up something valuable for another person's benefit or for a goal considered important.

examples.en: She sacrificed a free afternoon to help prepare the exhibition.
examples.vi: Cô ấy hy sinh một buổi chiều rảnh để giúp chuẩn bị triển lãm.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive sacrifice something for a purpose or to do something; does not always involve physical harm.
content.senseLabelEn: give up something valuable for a purpose

content.definitionEn: To tell someone about a possible danger or problem so that they can take care.

examples.en: The guide warned us about loose stones on the path.
examples.vi: Hướng dẫn viên cảnh báo chúng tôi về những viên đá không chắc trên lối đi.

content.grammarNotesEn: Warn someone about or of a danger; warn someone not to do something gives an instruction to avoid it.
content.meaningVi: cảnh báo; báo trước nguy cơ
content.senseLabelEn: tell someone about a possible risk

content.definitionEn: According to information received or to how a situation appears, without claiming certainty.

examples.en: Apparently, the afternoon train is running late.
examples.vi: Nghe nói chuyến tàu buổi chiều đang chạy muộn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Sentence adverb signals reported or apparent information; does not prove either truth or deliberate falsehood.
content.senseLabelEn: according to what is known or seems true

content.definitionEn: Relating to people rather than to other animals, machines, or things.

examples.en: The display explores human communication through images.
examples.vi: Khu trưng bày khám phá cách con người giao tiếp qua hình ảnh.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a noun such as communication or experience; this relational use does not deny that humans are animals biologically.
content.meaningVi: thuộc con người; của con người

content.definitionEn: A person; a member of the human species.

examples.en: The story describes a robot learning to work alongside humans.
examples.vi: Câu chuyện miêu tả một robot học cách làm việc cùng con người.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; humans is the regular plural, and human being is a related noun phrase.

content.definitionEn: The soft movable part inside the mouth used in tasting, moving food, and forming speech.

examples.en: She touched the loose tooth with her tongue.
examples.vi: Cô ấy dùng lưỡi chạm vào chiếc răng lung lay.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; the tongue can name the organ generally, while my tongue names a person's own.

content.definitionEn: A language, especially one associated with a person's home or community.

examples.en: His grandmother tells stories in her native tongue.
examples.vi: Bà của anh ấy kể chuyện bằng tiếng mẹ đẻ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; native tongue and mother tongue are established expressions. This language use is more literary than language alone.

content.definitionEn: A structure of fine threads made by a spider, often used to catch insects.

examples.en: A web stretched between the two branches above the path.
examples.vi: Một mạng nhện giăng giữa hai cành cây phía trên lối đi.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a spider's web names the structure, not the spider itself.

content.definitionEn: The system of connected pages and resources that people access through the internet.

examples.en: The museum put its opening hours on the web.
examples.vi: Bảo tàng đăng giờ mở cửa lên mạng web.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually the web in this sense; on the web describes online availability. Not every internet service is part of the web.
content.senseLabelEn: linked pages accessed through the internet

content.definitionEn: To work food between your teeth so that it becomes easier to swallow.

examples.en: He chewed the bread slowly while listening to the story.
examples.vi: Anh ấy nhai bánh mì chậm rãi trong lúc nghe câu chuyện.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive chew food or intransitive chew slowly; chew on can also name what is being bitten.

content.definitionEn: Done or experienced repeatedly as part of an established habit.

examples.en: Her habitual early arrival gave her time to unlock the hall.
examples.vi: Thói quen đến sớm thường lệ giúp cô ấy có thời gian mở khóa hội trường.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually before a noun such as behaviour or lateness; repetition does not itself imply addiction.

content.definitionEn: A road vehicle with two wheels that is powered by a motor.

examples.en: They parked the motorcycle beside the repair shop.
examples.vi: Họ đỗ xe máy cạnh tiệm sửa chữa.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; ride a motorcycle describes operating or travelling on it, rather than drive a motorcycle in ordinary usage.

content.definitionEn: Giving a feeling of enjoyment, comfort, or satisfaction.

examples.en: A pleasant breeze cooled the room after lunch.
examples.vi: Một làn gió dễ chịu làm căn phòng mát hơn sau bữa trưa.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a noun or after a linking verb; pleasant describes something enjoyable rather than someone experiencing pleasure.

content.definitionEn: A place where something stands, happens, or is planned to be built.

examples.en: The old factory site will become a public garden.
examples.vi: Khu đất của nhà máy cũ sẽ trở thành một khu vườn công cộng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; site of an event or site for a building specifies the use or association.

content.definitionEn: A website or collection of related pages available online.

examples.en: The charity's site lists places where volunteers are needed.
examples.vi: Trang web của tổ chức từ thiện liệt kê những nơi cần tình nguyện viên.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; visit a site describes online access here, not physical travel.

content.definitionEn: Extending to many parts of the world.

examples.en: The photograph attracted worldwide attention.
examples.vi: Bức ảnh thu hút sự chú ý trên toàn thế giới.

content.grammarNotesEn: Adjective before a noun; worldwide attention describes the geographical reach of interest.

content.definitionEn: In or to places across the world.

examples.en: The company sends its catalogue to readers worldwide.
examples.vi: Công ty gửi danh mục sản phẩm cho độc giả trên khắp thế giới.

content.grammarNotesEn: Adverb modifying distribution or activity; it does not literally require every country or individual.

content.definitionEn: A group of people gathered closely together in a place.

examples.en: A crowd gathered outside the station to welcome the musicians.
examples.vi: Một đám đông tụ tập ngoài nhà ga để chào đón các nhạc công.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable collective noun; a crowd of people specifies its members.

content.definitionEn: More or additional beyond what has already been given or done.

examples.en: Please contact the office for further details.
examples.vi: Hãy liên hệ văn phòng để biết thêm chi tiết.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually before a noun; further information is uncountable, while further questions is plural.

content.definitionEn: At or to a distance beyond the place already reached or mentioned.

examples.en: We walked further along the bank to find a shaded spot.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi đi xa hơn dọc bờ để tìm một chỗ có bóng mát.

content.grammarNotesEn: Adverb with movement or position; this draft concerns distance rather than an additional quantity.

content.definitionEn: Sounds arranged through rhythm, melody, or other patterns for expression or enjoyment.

examples.en: Soft music played while the guests found their seats.
examples.vi: Nhạc nhẹ vang lên trong lúc các vị khách tìm chỗ ngồi.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually uncountable; a piece of music names one work, rather than a music.
content.senseLabelEn: sounds arranged for expression or enjoyment

content.definitionEn: To tear or burst open, or cause something to do so.

examples.en: The frozen pipe ruptured during the night.
examples.vi: Đường ống bị đóng băng vỡ trong đêm.

content.grammarNotesEn: Intransitive when something ruptures; transitive when someone ruptures a material or structure.

content.definitionEn: The month that follows August and comes before October.

examples.en: The new reading club begins in September.
examples.vi: Câu lạc bộ đọc sách mới bắt đầu vào tháng Chín.

content.grammarNotesEn: Month name written September with a capital S; use in September, but on a particular September date.

content.definitionEn: Each time that something happens.

examples.en: Whenever the door opens, a small bell rings.
examples.vi: Mỗi khi cửa mở, một chiếc chuông nhỏ reo lên.

content.grammarNotesEn: Introduces a clause; the other clause describes what happens on each occasion.

content.definitionEn: At any time that a person chooses or that circumstances allow.

examples.en: You can return the book whenever you finish reading it.
examples.vi: Bạn có thể trả sách bất cứ khi nào đọc xong.

content.grammarNotesEn: Introduces a time clause; present finish can refer to a future occasion after can return.

content.definitionEn: Fine-grained earth that becomes easy to shape when mixed with water and is used for making pottery.

examples.en: The potter pressed the wet clay into a shallow dish.
examples.vi: Thợ gốm ép đất sét ướt thành một chiếc đĩa nông.

content.grammarNotesEn: Uncountable for the material; a piece or lump of clay names an amount.
content.senseLabelEn: fine earth that can be shaped when wet

content.definitionEn: The work or study of using scientific and practical knowledge to design, build, and improve structures or machines.

examples.en: She studies engineering and hopes to design safer bridges.
examples.vi: Cô ấy học ngành kỹ thuật và mong thiết kế những cây cầu an toàn hơn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Uncountable for the field; an engineering project names an application, not an engineering.
content.senseLabelEn: designing and building using technical knowledge

content.definitionEn: Happening or being done without intention, often because something was not noticed.

examples.en: An inadvertent change to the address sent the parcel to another street.
examples.vi: Một thay đổi vô ý ở địa chỉ khiến bưu kiện được gửi sang đường khác.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually before a noun such as error or omission; does not itself mean harmless.

content.definitionEn: To move your head briefly down and up, often to show agreement or recognition.

examples.en: She nodded to show that she had understood the instructions.
examples.vi: Cô ấy gật đầu để cho biết mình đã hiểu hướng dẫn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually intransitive; nod to someone identifies a recipient, and nod one's head uses an object.
content.senseLabelEn: move the head as a signal

content.definitionEn: To let your head drop briefly because you are sleepy.

examples.en: The passenger began to nod as the bus moved through the quiet streets.
examples.vi: Hành khách bắt đầu gật gù vì buồn ngủ khi xe buýt đi qua những con phố yên tĩnh.

content.grammarNotesEn: Intransitive; nod off means begin to fall asleep and is a related phrasal construction.
content.senseLabelEn: let the head drop when sleepy

content.definitionEn: A special chair used by a king, queen, or other ruler on formal occasions.

examples.en: The carved throne stood at the far end of the hall.
examples.vi: Chiếc ngai chạm khắc đặt ở cuối phía bên kia của đại sảnh.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable for the chair; the throne can also refer to royal authority in another use.

content.definitionEn: The measurement of something from one side to the other.

examples.en: Measure the width of the doorway before moving the desk.
examples.vi: Đo chiều rộng cửa ra vào trước khi chuyển chiếc bàn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually the width of something; a width of plus a measurement states its size.

content.definitionEn: A device or sound that warns people about danger or a situation needing attention.

examples.en: The alarm sounded when smoke reached the kitchen sensor.
examples.vi: Chuông báo động reo khi khói tới cảm biến trong bếp.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; set off an alarm means cause it to give a warning.
content.meaningVi: chuông báo động; thiết bị báo hiệu
content.senseLabelEn: device or sound giving a warning

content.definitionEn: To make someone feel worried or afraid about what may happen.

examples.en: The sudden drop in water pressure alarmed the caretaker.
examples.vi: Áp lực nước giảm đột ngột khiến người quản lý tòa nhà lo ngại.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive alarm someone; the cause is the subject and the worried person is the object.
content.meaningVi: làm lo ngại; làm hoảng sợ

content.definitionEn: A feeling of worry or fear when something seems dangerous or wrong.

examples.en: She watched with alarm as the branch bent over the road.
examples.vi: Cô ấy lo sợ nhìn cành cây cong xuống phía trên con đường.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually uncountable in with alarm or cause alarm; distinct from a warning device.
content.meaningVi: sự lo sợ; sự hoảng hốt

content.definitionEn: Used in and so forth to suggest more items of the kind already mentioned.

examples.en: Bring pencils, paper, glue, and so forth for the craft session.
examples.vi: Hãy mang bút chì, giấy, keo dán, vân vân cho buổi làm đồ thủ công.

content.grammarNotesEn: This sense occurs in the phrase and so forth after a list; forth alone does not mean et cetera.
content.meaningVi: vân vân; và những thứ tương tự

content.definitionEn: Out from a place or forwards from a starting point.

examples.en: Music came forth from the open doorway.
examples.vi: Tiếng nhạc vọng ra từ ô cửa đang mở.

content.grammarNotesEn: Formal or literary after movement or emergence verbs; back and forth describes repeated movement in opposite directions.
content.senseLabelEn: out or forwards from a place

content.definitionEn: To become greater in amount, size, or number, or make something greater.

examples.en: The library increased its opening hours during the exam period.
examples.vi: Thư viện tăng giờ mở cửa trong kỳ thi.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive increase something or intransitive something increases; increase by gives the change and increase to gives the new level.

content.definitionEn: A rise in the amount, size, or number of something.

examples.en: There was an increase in visitors after the exhibition opened.
examples.vi: Số khách tăng lên sau khi triển lãm mở cửa.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable in an increase in something; by/to distinguish the amount of change from the resulting level.

content.definitionEn: To go back to a place where you were before.

examples.en: We returned to the village before the evening rain.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi trở về làng trước cơn mưa chiều.

content.grammarNotesEn: Intransitive return to a place; return home has no to before home.
content.senseLabelEn: go back to an earlier place

content.definitionEn: The act of coming back to a place or situation.

examples.en: Her return to the choir pleased the other singers.
examples.vi: Việc cô ấy trở lại dàn hợp xướng khiến các ca sĩ khác vui mừng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually a return to something; possessive forms such as her return identify who comes back.
content.meaningVi: sự trở về; lần quay lại

content.definitionEn: To give or send something back to its owner or an earlier place.

examples.en: Please return the borrowed tools to the shed.
examples.vi: Hãy trả những dụng cụ đã mượn về nhà kho.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive return something to someone or somewhere; the object is what is given back.

content.definitionEn: To find a person, thing, or origin by following available signs or evidence.

examples.en: They traced the missing parcel to a neighbouring shop.
examples.vi: Họ lần theo dấu vết và tìm được bưu kiện thất lạc ở cửa hàng bên cạnh.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive trace something to a place or source; the endpoint is introduced by to.
content.meaningVi: truy tìm; lần theo dấu vết

content.definitionEn: A sign left by something that was present or happened earlier.

examples.en: The muddy floor showed traces of the visitors' boots.
examples.vi: Sàn nhà lấm bùn có dấu vết giày của các vị khách.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; traces of something are signs of its earlier presence.
content.senseLabelEn: small sign that something was present

content.definitionEn: A very small amount of a substance or quality.

examples.en: There was a trace of paint on his sleeve.
examples.vi: Có một vệt sơn rất nhỏ trên tay áo của anh ấy.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable in a trace of; emphasizes a small amount rather than a complete absence.

content.definitionEn: To copy a drawing by following its lines through or on another surface.

examples.en: She traced the leaf shape onto thin paper.
examples.vi: Cô ấy đồ lại hình chiếc lá lên giấy mỏng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive trace a shape onto a surface; distinct from finding something through evidence.

content.definitionEn: The process of becoming warmer or increasing in temperature.

examples.en: The warming of the room was gradual after the heater came on.
examples.vi: Căn phòng ấm dần lên sau khi máy sưởi bật.

content.grammarNotesEn: Uncountable process noun; warming of names what becomes warmer. Global warming is a specific context rather than the only meaning.
content.meaningVi: sự nóng lên; sự ấm lên

content.definitionEn: A person who controls a car or other road vehicle while it is moving.

examples.en: The driver waited until everyone had fastened their seat belt.
examples.vi: Tài xế chờ cho đến khi mọi người thắt dây an toàn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; driver of a vehicle names the person operating it, not every passenger.

content.definitionEn: Having the same or very similar composition or characteristics throughout.

examples.en: Stir the mixture until it looks homogeneous.
examples.vi: Khuấy hỗn hợp cho đến khi trông đồng nhất.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a noun or after a linking verb; homogeneity concerns uniform composition, not moral agreement.
content.meaningVi: đồng nhất; tương đối đồng đều

content.definitionEn: Not showing interest or concern about someone or something.

examples.en: He seemed indifferent to the choice of restaurant.
examples.vi: Anh ấy có vẻ không quan tâm đến việc chọn nhà hàng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Indifferent to names what causes little interest; this sense does not necessarily mean actively hostile.

content.definitionEn: A device that receives broadcasts of speech or music.

examples.en: She turned the radio down so she could hear the knock.
examples.vi: Cô ấy vặn nhỏ tiếng đài để nghe tiếng gõ cửa.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable for the device; turn the radio down reduces volume, not its physical position.

content.definitionEn: The medium of broadcasting sound programmes to listeners.

examples.en: The interview will be broadcast on local radio tomorrow.
examples.vi: Cuộc phỏng vấn sẽ được phát trên đài địa phương vào ngày mai.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually uncountable; on the radio refers to broadcast availability rather than a device's surface.

content.definitionEn: A person's own identity, character, and inner experience.

examples.en: The journal helped her understand her own self more clearly.
examples.vi: Cuốn nhật ký giúp cô ấy hiểu bản thân rõ hơn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable in phrases such as one's true self; selves is the plural. This noun differs from reflexive pronouns such as herself.
content.meaningVi: bản thân; con người bên trong

content.definitionEn: Made from wood.

examples.en: A wooden bench stood under the old mango tree.
examples.vi: Một chiếc ghế dài bằng gỗ đặt dưới cây xoài già.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a noun or after a linking verb; this material sense differs from wooden meaning stiff or unexpressive.

content.definitionEn: A member of a council that makes decisions for a local area.

examples.en: The councillor listened to residents' concerns about the crossing.
examples.vi: Thành viên hội đồng địa phương lắng nghe lo ngại của cư dân về chỗ qua đường.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; British spelling councillor, American councilor. Counsellor refers to a different role.
content.meaningVi: thành viên hội đồng địa phương; nghị viên địa phương

content.definitionEn: To consider evidence in order to judge the quality, value, or effectiveness of something.

examples.en: The teachers evaluated the new timetable after a month.
examples.vi: Các giáo viên đánh giá thời khóa biểu mới sau một tháng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive evaluate something; evaluation may examine strengths and weaknesses, not only assign a score.

content.definitionEn: Among the most important, successful, or influential in a particular area.

examples.en: A leading researcher spoke at the public lecture.
examples.vi: Một nhà nghiên cứu hàng đầu phát biểu tại buổi diễn thuyết công cộng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually before a noun; a leading person need not be the only leader or the person physically in front.
content.senseLabelEn: among the most important or successful

content.definitionEn: The act of watching something carefully to learn about it.

examples.en: Careful observation revealed which birds visited the garden first.
examples.vi: Sự quan sát kỹ cho thấy những loài chim nào đến khu vườn trước.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually uncountable for the process; observation of names what is watched.

content.definitionEn: A comment about something that someone has noticed.

examples.en: Her observation about the crowded entrance led us to move the sign.
examples.vi: Nhận xét của cô ấy về lối vào đông đúc khiến chúng tôi chuyển biển chỉ dẫn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; make an observation about something introduces a particular comment.

content.definitionEn: The number that is one greater than twelve.

examples.en: Thirteen chairs fitted around the long table.
examples.vi: Mười ba chiếc ghế kê vừa quanh chiếc bàn dài.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a plural count noun or used alone as a number; thirteen chairs takes plural agreement.

content.definitionEn: To form written words or compose a text using handwriting, typing, or another writing method.

examples.en: She wrote a short note explaining where the keys were.
examples.vi: Cô ấy viết một ghi chú ngắn giải thích chìa khóa ở đâu.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive write a text; write to someone names the recipient. Past wrote and past participle written.

content.definitionEn: An unexpected event that causes damage, injury, or another unwanted result.

examples.en: A minor accident blocked the narrow road for an hour.
examples.vi: Một tai nạn nhỏ làm tắc con đường hẹp trong một giờ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; have an accident names the event, while by accident expresses lack of intention.
content.senseLabelEn: unexpected event causing damage or injury

content.definitionEn: Something that happens by chance rather than being planned.

examples.en: Meeting her at the book fair was a happy accident.
examples.vi: Gặp cô ấy ở hội chợ sách là một sự tình cờ vui vẻ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable in a happy accident; by accident means unintentionally and need not involve injury.
content.meaningVi: sự tình cờ; chuyện ngoài dự định

content.definitionEn: Relating to a system in which a central government shares authority with constituent states, or to that central government.

examples.en: The class compared federal and local responsibilities in a fictional country.
examples.vi: Lớp học so sánh trách nhiệm của chính quyền liên bang và địa phương ở một quốc gia giả định.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually before a noun such as government or authority; not a synonym for every national government.
content.senseLabelEn: relating to a federation's central government

content.definitionEn: To make someone feel afraid or less confident, sometimes to influence their behaviour.

examples.en: The aggressive questions intimidated the new speaker.
examples.vi: Những câu hỏi gay gắt khiến người diễn giả mới mất tự tin.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive intimidate someone; intimidate someone into doing something names an action induced by pressure.
content.meaningVi: đe dọa; làm sợ; gây áp lực khiến mất tự tin
content.senseLabelEn: make someone afraid or less confident

content.definitionEn: A team sport in which players carry, pass, and kick an oval ball to score.

examples.en: The school rugby team practised passing on the field.
examples.vi: Đội rugby của trường tập chuyền bóng trên sân.

content.grammarNotesEn: Uncountable when naming the sport; a rugby match is countable. Rugby is distinct from American football.
content.meaningVi: môn rugby; bóng bầu dục rugby
content.senseLabelEn: team sport with an oval ball

content.definitionEn: Easily affected by emotions, criticism, or how others behave.

examples.en: She is sensitive to criticism about her artwork.
examples.vi: Cô ấy nhạy cảm với những lời phê bình về tác phẩm của mình.

content.grammarNotesEn: Sensitive to names the cause of an emotional response; does not necessarily mean unreasonable.
content.meaningVi: nhạy cảm; dễ bị tổn thương về cảm xúc
content.senseLabelEn: easily affected by feelings or treatment

content.definitionEn: Able to detect or be affected by small changes or particular conditions.

examples.en: The sensor is sensitive to small changes in light.
examples.vi: Cảm biến nhạy với những thay đổi nhỏ của ánh sáng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Sensitive to identifies the stimulus; the subject may be a device, material, or body part.

content.definitionEn: Showing sound judgment based on understanding or experience.

examples.en: It was wise to check the route before leaving.
examples.vi: Kiểm tra lộ trình trước khi đi là một việc làm sáng suốt.

content.grammarNotesEn: A wise decision or it is wise to do something evaluates judgment; not restricted to older people.

content.definitionEn: A plan showing how something should look, be built, or function.
